items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: oh guys, like Lang, you know Lang. I can't remember. Lang was playing with George Louis that, a little bright fellow, a red fellow who played the piano so much.

ctx.x: I have that one you made with Bunk. We can play it after a while if you have it. Yeah. We'll be through here in about five minutes. Yeah, so. I was going to ask about the rhythm section. What kind of a rhythm section would you rather work with? A guitar or banjo or piano or what? If I had to work? Yeah. And the drummer, I mean how big a section would you rather have? Piano and drums and guitar or banjo, how big a rhythm section?

You know, I'll tell you why. I'd rather work just with the ghetto, if I got a good ghetto player. You see, you're going to take trouble to find a piano player going to work with the ghetto, bass, and the drums. You see, you don't get all piano players to work with, you know, the way you support. You see, it's a different thing. Like, I can't say what I want to say. But anyhow, if you've got a piano player that understands, you'd like some of these, oh guys, like Lang, you know Lang. I can't remember. Lang was…
No, I don't think I knew him. Anyway, go ahead. So that's where, oh you take, well somebody, you got to be together on those things, you
